global.headline: IRAN — TRUMP SAYS TALKS WILL CONTINUE BUT CEASEFIRE "OVER"; US DEMANDS PUBLIC HORMUZ GUARANTEE AS ISRAEL WARNS OF FRESH PLOT ON TRUMP
summary: After two consecutive nights of large-scale US strikes and Iranian retaliation against four Gulf states, 10 July brought a relative lull and a diplomatic scramble. Trump wrote on Truth Social that "the Islamic Republic of Iran has asked us to continue 'talks.' We have agreed to do so, but the United States has stated to them, in no uncertain terms, that the Cease Fire is OVER!" — a formulation that keeps negotiations alive while insisting the June MOU's truce itself has lapsed, with no formal termination notice filed by either side. Senior US officials said Washington expects Tehran to shortly issue a public statement declaring the Strait of Hormuz open and guaranteeing commercial vessels will not be attacked; Qatari negotiators were in Tehran discussing both the navigation dispute and the wider MOU. Qatar's foreign ministry reaffirmed "diplomacy and mediation as the path towards resolving conflicts," with Pakistan and other regional mediators also engaged.

Despite the diplomatic movement, actual Hormuz traffic remained frozen: Lloyd's List Intelligence recorded no vessel above 10,000 dwt transiting the US-coordinated Southern Highway route with its AIS switched on since 7 July, though LNG tankers continued to pass. Oil eased on the prospect of a reopening — Brent fell 0.5% to $75.92/barrel and WTI dropped 0.96% to $71.39 on 10 July — but both were still tracking a roughly 5-6% weekly gain given the week's strikes. Separately, Israel shared intelligence with Washington that Iranian hardliners, reportedly including new IRGC commander Ahmad Vahidi, want to assassinate Trump; US officials cautioned this reflects a desire among hardliners rather than an operational plan Iran's leadership has approved, and some officials suspect Israel is using the intelligence to influence Trump's decisions on further strikes. Mojtaba Khamenei's public absence, unbroken since the funeral period, remains the central unresolved signal of who is directing Iran's response.

Iranian attacks on Jordan this week also exposed the kingdom's difficult position — hosting US, German, Belgian and French forces at Al Azraq while trying to avoid becoming a combatant in a war not its own. No new Iranian strikes or US strikes were reported to have hit Iranian or regional targets within this 24-hour window, the first such pause since the ceasefire's practical collapse began 7-8 July.
global.geopolitical: The choreography of "talks continue, ceasefire is over" lets both sides claim they haven't capitulated while quietly de-escalating — Washington gets a public Hormuz guarantee it can point to, Tehran avoids the appearance of caving after two nights of strikes. But it is a verbal de-escalation only: traffic through the strait has not moved, and the Israeli-sourced assassination-plot intelligence, however uncertain its provenance or motive, adds a volatile new variable that could reverse the lull in an instant if Trump credits it.
global.socioeconomic: A pause in strikes rather than a resolution is enough to pull oil back from the week's surge, underlining how jumpy the market remains around any signal — real or rhetorical — out of the strait. For Singapore, the compounding effects tracked all week (record Q3 electricity tariff, downgraded tourism forecast, stranded seafarers) are unchanged until vessels actually start moving again; a Hormuz-open statement without traffic to match it would be a headline, not a fix.

global.headline: SOUTHERN SPAIN WILDFIRE KILLS AT LEAST 12, 23 MISSING — DEADLIEST IN OVER TWO DECADES
summary: A fast-moving wildfire tore through a remote expatriate community near the Sierra de los Filabres mountains in Almeria province overnight Thursday into Friday, killing at least 12 people and leaving 23 unaccounted for as of Friday — Spain's deadliest wildfire in more than 20 years. Most victims died after ignoring shelter-in-place instructions; some tried to flee along a dry riverbed that turned into what officials called a "death trap" as flames closed in from multiple directions. Four of the dead are believed to be British nationals, identified in part from the right-hand-drive steering wheels of their burned-out cars.

Sixteen aircraft were deployed Friday alongside ground crews continuing search-and-rescue operations for the missing. Officials cited a combination of prolonged drought, high winds and extreme heat as the worst possible fire conditions the region has faced this season.
global.geopolitical: A significant British casualty toll in an EU member state during peak summer travel season puts pressure on both Madrid and London over evacuation protocols for large expatriate and tourist populations in wildfire-prone areas — a recurring gap as southern Europe's fire seasons intensify.
global.socioeconomic: Almeria's wildfire adds to a summer of extreme-heat and fire damage across southern Europe, with knock-on costs to tourism-dependent local economies and insurance markets already absorbing a run of climate-driven disaster claims.

global.headline: TYPHOON BAVI: PHILIPPINES LANDSLIDES KILL AT LEAST 15 AS STORM HEADS FOR TAIWAN AND SOUTH CHINA
summary: Landslides triggered by Typhoon Bavi's outer rain bands killed at least 15 people and left six missing on Mindanao in the southern Philippines — 10 in a landslide that hit Malapatan in Sarangani province and at least five in a separate slide in Lanao del Sur. Bavi, one of the largest storms in decades at roughly 1,000km across at its widest, weakened as it crossed the Philippine Sea near Northern Luzon but remains on a track toward Taiwan, remote Japanese islands and south-eastern China, where it is expected to make landfall Saturday.

More than 2,000 people have been evacuated in Taiwan, mostly from the mountainous Hualien county, where authorities are monitoring two barrier dams for potential dam-break flooding as the storm approaches.
global.geopolitical: A storm this size crossing multiple jurisdictions in quick succession tests disaster-coordination capacity across the Philippines, Taiwan, Japan and China simultaneously, at a moment when regional attention is heavily consumed by the Iran crisis.
global.socioeconomic: Mindanao's landslide toll adds to a pattern of deadly slope failures in the southern Philippines during heavy monsoon and typhoon rain; Taiwan's dam monitoring and evacuations point to renewed flood-damage exposure just as the island manages other economic pressures from the Iran-linked shipping disruption.

global.headline: HOUSTON: WITNESSES DISPUTE ICE ACCOUNT OF FATAL SHOOTING OF MAN WHO WAS NOT THE TARGET
summary: Three men who were in the van with Lorenzo Salgado Araujo when he was fatally shot by an ICE agent this week said in a Friday news conference, through their attorney, that he never tried to run over anyone and that agents fired into the van from the side — directly contradicting ICE's account that Salgado Araujo "weaponised his vehicle in an attempt to run over an ICE law enforcement officer," prompting the officer to fire in "self-defense." The witnesses said no agent was ever standing in front of the vehicle or in its path. DHS has said the agents involved were not wearing body cameras, citing lapses in federal funding, and no video of the shooting itself has surfaced publicly.

Salgado Araujo does not appear to have been ICE's intended target that morning; a Homeland Security official said agents had surveilled a specific property for weeks and stopped his van because the driver resembled the person they were looking for.
global.geopolitical: A wrongful-target fatal shooting with contested facts and no body-camera footage adds to friction points in the Trump administration's expanded immigration-enforcement posture, feeding into diplomatic friction with Mexico, which separately said this week it will file complaints in the US over a string of Mexican deaths linked to ICE operations.
global.socioeconomic: The absence of body cameras, attributed to funding lapses, is likely to become a flashpoint in oversight and litigation over the case regardless of how the shooting itself is eventually adjudicated, with implications for how future ICE use-of-force incidents are documented and contested.

global.headline: SK HYNIX RAISES US$26.5B IN LARGEST-EVER FOREIGN US LISTING, RIDING THE AI CHIP BOOM
summary: South Korea's SK Hynix priced 177.9 million American depositary shares at US$149 each, raising US$26.5 billion (~S$35.7 billion) in the largest-ever US listing by a non-American company — surpassing Alibaba's 2014 US$25 billion debut and ranking second globally only to SpaceX's US$85.7 billion Nasdaq listing in June. Shares opened Friday under the temporary ticker SKHYV roughly 14% above the IPO price and kept climbing through the session; regular trading under ticker SKHY begins Monday.

SK Hynix said proceeds will fund new production facilities in South Korea to meet AI-driven demand for high-bandwidth memory chips used in Nvidia and other AI accelerators — a company that was near collapse a decade ago now positioned as one of the AI boom's central beneficiaries.
global.geopolitical: A South Korean chipmaker choosing a US listing over its home Seoul exchange for this scale of capital-raising signals how tightly the AI-chip supply chain is now bound to US capital markets even as manufacturing capacity expansion is directed back to Korea, a dynamic Washington will likely cite in pushing SK Hynix toward eventual US fab investment too.
global.socioeconomic: The listing is a fresh data point for sovereign investors like Temasek weighing AI-sector exposure (already tracked at ~6% of its portfolio, targeting up to 15% by 2031) — a record-breaking chip IPO this soon after SpaceX's suggests AI-infrastructure valuations remain resilient even amid the Iran-driven volatility hitting energy and shipping markets.

singapore.headline: JOHOR GOES TO THE POLLS: STATE ELECTION SEEN AS BELLWETHER FOR JS-SEZ MOMENTUM AND SINGAPORE COST-OF-LIVING HEDGE
summary: Voters across Johor cast ballots Saturday for all 56 seats in the state legislative assembly, in a contest framed by regional commentators as a test of whether Malaysia's southernmost state can hold its pragmatic, investment-friendly political line even as the peninsula trends toward more conservative, nationalist politics elsewhere. Malaysia's immigration authorities set up a special taskforce and dedicated lanes at Singapore-Johor checkpoints to manage voting-day crossings, reflecting how deeply the two economies are now intertwined — hundreds of thousands of Johoreans commute to work in Singapore, and Johor has become both a weekend destination and, increasingly, a cost-of-living hedge for Singaporeans priced out of the city-state.

The outcome carries direct stakes for the Johor-Singapore Special Economic Zone (JS-SEZ), the Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link timeline and continued foreign investment confidence — all of which assume a stable Johor state government able to keep delivering on cross-border commitments without political distraction.
singapore.geopolitical: A result that preserves Johor's pluralistic, business-friendly coalition would reassure Singapore and foreign investors betting on JS-SEZ; a swing toward the more nationalist bloc gaining ground elsewhere in Malaysia would inject fresh uncertainty into RTS Link delivery and cross-border planning just as both governments have been talking up the zone's momentum.
singapore.socioeconomic: For ordinary Singaporeans, the vote is a proxy for whether the informal bet many are placing — treating Johor Bahru as an extension of Singapore for housing, groceries and leisure to offset domestic cost-of-living pressure — remains a sound one, or whether political uncertainty across the Causeway complicates it.

singapore.headline: MSF FAMILY TRENDS REPORT: MARRIAGES DOWN 6.2% IN 2025, SENIORS LIVING ALONE DOUBLE IN A DECADE
summary: The Ministry of Social and Family Development's Family Trends Report 2025 found marriages fell 6.2% in 2025 from 2024, continuing a decline that saw 2024 registrations already down 7% year-on-year. The number of residents aged 65 and above living alone has roughly doubled over the past decade, from 42,100 in 2014 to 87,200 in 2024, though MSF noted 80% of seniors still live with a spouse or children. On a brighter note, government-paid paternity leave uptake rose from 47% of eligible fathers (for children born in 2016) to 61% (children born in 2024), and shared parental leave was expanded from six to ten weeks from 1 April 2026.
MSF separately highlighted improving marriage stability, with dissolution rates declining among more recent marriage cohorts even as fewer marriages are being registered overall.
singapore.geopolitical: None material — a domestic demographic report.
singapore.socioeconomic: The figures sit squarely inside the same demographic trend this briefing already tracks via the 2025 total fertility rate of 0.87, a historic low — fewer marriages compound the fertility problem directly, while the doubling of seniors living alone adds a distinct eldercare and social-support planning burden even as paternity-leave uptake shows some of the government's family-support policies gaining traction on the margin.

singapore.headline: HDB: PARTS OF MAJU FOREST IN CLEMENTI TO MAKE WAY FOR NEW PUBLIC HOUSING ESTATE
summary: HDB announced plans on 10 July to redevelop part of the 23-hectare Maju Forest, bounded by Brookvale Drive, Clementi Road and Sunset Way, into a new public housing estate — about 15 hectares released for development while roughly 8 hectares, including a freshwater stream and high-biodiversity vegetation, will be retained to provide wildlife refuge and habitat connectivity. A new roughly 4km Old Jurong Line nature trail is being studied alongside the existing 2km Clementi Nature Trail. Public feedback on the plans is open from 10 July to 6 August; details on unit numbers and timeline are still to come.
The announcement is part of the same broader HDB land-release push that separately includes redevelopment plans for Gillman Barracks and Sunset Way.
singapore.geopolitical: None material — a domestic land-use announcement.
singapore.socioeconomic: Another entry in the government's push to expand housing supply against a backdrop of a first resale-price decline since 2019 and continued high demand; the retained-forest compromise also signals HDB is trying to manage green-space and biodiversity pushback more visibly than in some past land releases.

singapore.headline: 69 INVESTIGATED, INCLUDING 15-YEAR-OLD, IN CROSS-BORDER UNLICENSED MONEYLENDING CRACKDOWN
summary: Singapore Police said 69 people aged 15 to 76 are under investigation following a week-long islandwide operation (1-7 July) against unlicensed moneylending: nine allegedly harassed debtors at their homes, 15 acted as runners conducting ATM transfers, and 36 allegedly opened bank accounts and handed over ATM cards, PINs or internet-banking tokens to loan sharks. Acting on a tip from Malaysian counterparts, police are separately probing nine people aged 18-67 for suspected cross-border moneylending, allegedly supplying phone numbers and bank accounts to unlicensed lenders operating in both countries.
singapore.geopolitical: The cross-border cooperation with Malaysian police on this operation is a small but concrete example of the kind of bilateral law-enforcement coordination that underpins the broader Singapore-Malaysia relationship now in focus with Johor's state election.
singapore.socioeconomic: A 15-year-old among those investigated underscores how unlicensed moneylending and scam syndicates are increasingly recruiting minors as runners and mule-account holders — a recruitment pattern police have flagged repeatedly as scam losses climb nationally.

word.definition: A friendly, often informal understanding or basis for cooperation between states or factions, falling short of a formal alliance or treaty.
word.etymology: From French entente ("understanding"), from Old French entente ("intent, purpose"), from the past participle of entendre ("to understand, to intend") — ultimately from Latin intendere ("to stretch toward, to direct one's attention"). Entered English diplomatic vocabulary via entente cordiale, the informal early-20th-century Anglo-French understanding.
word.example: The uneasy entente Qatari and Pakistani mediators managed to hold together on 10 July — talks resuming even as Trump insisted the ceasefire was "over" — was thin enough that a single contested piece of Israeli intelligence about a plot against Trump could unravel it by morning.
